text:
ConocoPhillips dropped 4.7% today after crude oil prices reversed course sharply. On Monday, oil had sold off more than 7% on optimism about U.S.-Iran peace talks, but that momentum reversed when the U.S. carried out military strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island on Monday—a reminder that the diplomatic path remains uncertain. Oil prices climbed back in response to the strike, but the company's stock fell anyway, suggesting investors were spooked by the renewed military escalation and the unpredictability it introduces into energy markets.

The broader picture adds context: rival oil majors like BP and Saudi Aramco posted blowout earnings this quarter because refining margins—the spread between crude costs and finished fuel prices—have surged amid Middle East tensions. ConocoPhillips should benefit from the same tailwind, yet today's selloff reflects the market's anxiety about whether the current volatility is sustainable or a temporary spike that could evaporate if genuine diplomacy takes hold.
